paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. You can't lean on the wrong things and expect them to hold you up. The watchmen were blind, the shepherds were chasing "his own gain," and the idols couldn't save anybody (Isa 56:10-11; 57:13). God says "the wind will carry off all of them, a breath will take them away." But "he who seeks refuge in Me will inherit the land and possess My holy mountain" (Isa 57:13).

Now here's the part that gets me. The One who is "high and lifted up" says He dwells "with the oppressed and humble in spirit, to restore the spirit of the lowly and revive the heart of the contrite" (Isa 57:15). He says, "I have seen his ways, but I will heal him" (Isa 57:18). Friend, God sees the whole mess and still says HEAL. I spent years in a junk drawer thinking nobody would ever reach back there, so that kind of mercy hits me right in the apron.

So what do you do with it? You run to Him instead of running around. The storm-tossed sea "cannot be still," but God says, "Peace, peace to those far and near" (Isa 57:19-20). Whatever you've been chasing to feel steady, set it down and take refuge in Him. His peace is the real thing, and you don't have to earn it.
